metrics.outcome: Done: the site is workable. Every done-when item passes with Audit's evidence and the render check is clean.
metrics.brief: make a website for my aunt's flower shop called Petal & Stem in Jaipur. people should see the bouquets with prices, order one for delivery, and know the shop timings and where it is

review.verdict: Clean first-pass build (8 of 8 done-when, 1 cycle, 70 of 100 budget, 0 redirects), but the brief was too easy to test negotiation, conflict, rework or lesson reuse.

identity.note: Got everything in one question round [2], recorded a tight charter [5], and disclosed the unrequested phrases [25]. Docked: no stated ship-or-fix decision on Audit's two warnings, and the delivery areas it asked about [2] were never answered and are not in dropped_from_brief.

adaptation.note: Reused a cafe playbook, trimmed to four workflows with 30 held back [7]. Saving a lesson after a first-pass success [26] goes beyond its file (lesson after a confirmed fix), but is sensible.

priority.note: Granted all four with a checkable reserve (3 fixes at 8) [8]. Its pushback was never tested, and the envelope checks [11,14,17,20] read as templated.

coordination.note: Stated the scheduling rule and lock each time [10,13,16,19]; no collisions. HOLD never came up. Messages look templated (double period), so part of this score is code.

audit.note: Found two defects the code check missed [24]. Weak: R-1 is never explained, the warnings name no criterion, and it does not mention the invented phrases Identity raised [25].

W-1.note: Scaffold, viewport meta, nav, hero [12]. Its style guide did not cover form controls (Arial button [24]). Source of the duplicate title is not shown (unverified).

W-2.note: Exactly five bouquets, exact prices, empty placeholders [15]. No finding against it.

W-3.note: Form and wa.me link built [18]. Button fell back to Arial [24]. No evidence the WhatsApp text carries the entered details.

W-4.note: Delivery terms, timings, address, tap-to-call and map link in two sections [21]. No finding against it.

went_well: No redirects, invalid moves, validator rejections or role refusals across 19 turns (metrics).
The code check [23] covered overflow at 360/1280px, JS errors and links before Audit, leaving Audit the judgment calls.
Workflow agents labelled their claims 'not browser-tested' [12,15,18,21] instead of asserting a pass.
problems: Two low defects shipped (duplicate <title>, Arial button) [24] with 30 budget left and fixes priced at 8 [8]. Identity closed [25] with no recorded ship-or-fix call.
Invented copy ('fresh flowers', 'Bouquets for every occasion') entered a facts-only site [25]. [24] does not list it.
Counters disagree with the chat: lessons saved/used are empty though [7] and [26] show both; warnings are 0 though [24] reports 3; 15 AI calls vs 19 turns.
Charged equals estimate for all four workflows, so the budget says nothing about estimate accuracy.
learnings: Change: only W-1 writes head tags. builder.md lets every builder do it, and a duplicate title appeared [24].
Change: W-1's style guide must cover form controls, and the code check needs a form-font test. It said 'no problems' [23] while Audit found the Arial fallback [24].
Change: audit.md says send fixable defects to Adaptation; team.md only allows Audit to Identity. Keep Audit to Identity, and make Identity's done message list each open warning as fix or ship.
Change: decide whether generic taglines count as 'invented'. Either say they are allowed in the charter or have Audit check them.
Test system: fix the lessons, warnings and call counters before comparing runs. Add actual calls per workflow against envelope limits; the budget is rate card only.

Test next: same brief at start budget 40 (forces COUNTER/REFUSE); a brief missing the WhatsApp number (to_be_confirmed); a brief asking for online payment (charter conflict); a planted defect to see if Audit catches it. This one run gives no evidence on conflict, HOLD, retry, rework or lesson reuse.
Keep: playbook reuse across business types (cafe to florist [7]). One run, so not proven.
